sections.skill: Keep a series consistent and request targeted edits

questions.prompt: What is drift in an image series?

choices.text: Details changing from one image to the next
Images slowly moving across the screen when you scroll through the pages of a book

questions.correct_answer: Details changing from one image to the next
questions.intro: When you need a SERIES of images, such as a character on every page of a story or slides with one look, generators often drift: hair color changes, a shirt gets new stripes, the art style shifts. To keep CONSISTENCY, reuse the same detailed description each time ("Mia: short curly black hair, yellow raincoat, round glasses"), keep the same style words, and use reference-image features if your tool has them. For EDITS, ask for one TARGETED change ("make only the raincoat green; keep everything else") instead of redescribing the whole image, and compare the result with the original.

sections.skill: Compare a series with a school uniform

questions.prompt: What does a uniform keep the same?
questions.correct_answer: Colors, clothes and logo
questions.intro: A school uniform keeps students looking alike: same colors, same shirt, same logo every day. If each student chose their own outfit daily, photos from the year would look mismatched. A character in a series of images needs a "uniform" too: the same written description of hair, clothes and colors, used every time, so the character looks like the same person on every page.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Catch edits that change too much

questions.prompt: You asked to change the sky, and the person's face also changed. What does this show?

choices.text: That the sky and face are the same
That the tool always changes faces on purpose whenever you ask it to change the sky
Edits can change more than asked

questions.correct_answer: Edits can change more than asked
questions.intro: Edits can change more than you asked: a request to change the background may also change a face or move objects. Check the whole image after each edit, not just the part you changed. Keep a copy of each version so you can go back. For a long series, write a short "style sheet" listing each character's features, the colors and the style, and check each new image against it before accepting it.

questions.prompt: Why keep a copy of each version during edits?
